verdict.summary: YouTube scopes are treated as sensitive, so a public app needs Google OAuth verification (typically 3–5 business days) before it can drop the unverified warning and the 100-user cap. Separately, every project is capped at 10,000 units/day plus 100 search.list and 100 videos.insert calls, and the only way past that is a manual YouTube API compliance audit with no published timeline and a real chance of rejection for analytics- or scraping-like use cases.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create a Cloud project, enable YouTube Data API v3, set up the consent screen in Testing with test users, and create a web OAuth client. No review needed.

timeToProd.assumes: An agent that reads channel/video data for many users and needs more than the default quota, so it needs both sensitive-scope verification and a quota audit. If 10,000 units/day is enough, only OAuth verification applies (about 1–3 weeks).
timeToProd.waitingOn: Google Trust & Safety sensitive-scope verification, then the YouTube API Services compliance audit and quota extension review.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Google states 3–5 business days for sensitive verification. YouTube's audit page only says the team will reach out 'as soon as possible'. The several-weeks-to-months audit range is from a third-party guide.

prerequisites.item: A Google Cloud project with YouTube Data API v3 enabled
prerequisites.why: Quota, OAuth clients and the audit are all tied to the project.

prerequisites.item: A verified domain with a public homepage and privacy policy on the same domain
prerequisites.why: Sensitive-scope verification requires Search Console domain verification and a privacy policy linked from the consent screen.

prerequisites.item: A YouTube-compliant privacy policy and data handling
prerequisites.why: YouTube policies require users to agree to a privacy policy, a link to Google's security settings for revocation, deletion within 7 days of in-app revocation, and refresh or deletion of stored data every 30 days.

prerequisites.item: A demo video uploaded to YouTube as Unlisted
prerequisites.why: Verification asks for a video showing the consent flow and how each sensitive scope is used.

scopeTiers.tier: Public data with an API key (no OAuth)
scopeTiers.impact: Public videos, channels, playlists and comments can be read with an API key, with no consent screen. Default quota limits still apply and storage limits for non-authorized data are 30 days.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Unauthenticated calls are rejected; an API key or OAuth identity is required (observed live).

scopeTiers.impact: Lets an agent list the user's channel, playlists, subscriptions and ratings. Needs sensitive-scope verification for public use; otherwise test users only, with 7-day refresh tokens, or a lifetime cap of 100 users behind the unverified warning.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Google's docs use 'deleting a YouTube video' as a sensitive-scope example but don't publish a per-scope table; the sensitive classification of youtube.readonly comes from third-party sources. Check the Data Access page in Cloud Console.

scopeTiers.impact: Write access: post comments, edit metadata, upload. Same verification path, with stronger justification needed for each scope. Uploads are capped at 100 videos.insert calls per day per project.
For YouTube partners and content owners. Most AI agents don't need these. Membership data is creator-only.
Needed once you outgrow 10,000 units/day or 100 search.list calls/day. Extra quota may only be used for the approved use case; a changed use case needs a new audit.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Timeline is from a third-party guide; Google publishes none.

steps.title: Create a Cloud project and enable YouTube Data API v3
steps.detail: Create or pick a Google Cloud project and enable YouTube Data API v3 in the API Library.

steps.title: Configure branding, audience and data access
steps.detail: In Google Auth Platform, set app name, support email, homepage and privacy policy; add test users; declare the YouTube scopes you'll request.

steps.title: Create a web OAuth client and build the flow
steps.detail: Use https://accounts.google.com/o/oauth2/v2/auth with access_type=offline and the narrowest YouTube scope, then exchange at https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token. Use incremental authorization for write scopes.

steps.title: Budget quota per feature
steps.detail: Map each agent action to its bucket: search.list (100 calls/day), videos.insert (100 calls/day), videos.batchGetStats (own 10,000/day bucket), everything else from 10,000 units/day. Cache aggressively within the 30-day storage limit.

steps.title: Draft the privacy policy and YouTube compliance features
steps.detail: Write a policy covering YouTube data access, a link to https://myaccount.google.com/permissions, 30-day refresh/delete, 7-day deletion after revocation, and a contact method. Add an in-app disconnect that revokes the token.

steps.title: Verify the domain and record the demo video
steps.detail: Verify every authorized domain in Search Console, then record the end-to-end consent flow showing each scope in use and upload it to YouTube as Unlisted.

steps.title: Submit for sensitive-scope verification
steps.detail: Publish the app and submit verification with the scope justifications the agent drafted.

steps.title: Wait for Google verification
steps.detail: Google says sensitive verification typically takes 3–5 business days; respond quickly to Trust & Safety emails.

steps.title: Submit the YouTube Audit and Quota Extension Form
steps.detail: Describe the use case, show the product (screenshots or test account), and estimate quota per method. Incomplete forms delay processing.

steps.title: Wait for the compliance audit
steps.detail: A YouTube API Services team member contacts you; they may ask for account access to all features. Approved quota can be lower than requested.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Duration from a third-party guide; Google gives no SLA.

agentCanDo: Pick the narrowest scope per feature and write scope justifications
Estimate daily quota per method and draft the audit form answers
Implement token revocation and 30-day refresh/delete jobs
humanMustDo: Create the Cloud project and OAuth client
Verify domain ownership in Search Console
Record and upload the demo video
Submit Google verification and the YouTube audit form
Give YouTube reviewers test account access if asked

blockers.symptom: 403 quotaExceeded after a few dozen searches
blockers.cause: search.list now has its own bucket of 100 calls/day per project, separate from the 10,000-unit pool.
blockers.fix: Cache search results, prefer playlistItems/channels lookups, or request more search quota through the audit form.

blockers.symptom: 'Google hasn't verified this app' warning on consent
blockers.cause: App is published with YouTube scopes but hasn't passed sensitive-scope verification.
blockers.fix: Complete verification. Until then, at most 100 new users can ever pass the warning for this project.

blockers.symptom: Refresh tokens stop working after 7 days
blockers.cause: App is in Testing mode; test-user authorizations expire seven days after consent.
blockers.fix: Publish the app to Production (and verify) for long-lived refresh tokens.

blockers.symptom: Audit rejected or granted much less quota than requested
blockers.cause: Use case looks like bulk harvesting, competitive analytics or scraping, or stores/derives data in ways the policies forbid.
blockers.fix: Narrow the use case to user-authorized data, drop derived metrics, and resubmit or appeal via the appeals form.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Rejection patterns from a third-party guide; derived-data ban is in official policy.

blockers.cause: Call made with neither an API key nor an OAuth token.
blockers.fix: Send an API key for public data or a Bearer token for user data.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed live on GET https://www.googleapis.com/youtube/v3/channels?part=id&mine=true without credentials.

nuances.text: Authorized data can be stored for at most 30 days before you refresh or delete it; analytics data can be kept longer but you must recheck authorization every 30 days. Since June 2026, audited analytics developers can request to store some statistics longer.

YouTube policies forbid using API data to create new or derived data or metrics, which matters for agents that summarize or score channels. A separate derived-metrics policy applies only to audited analytics developers.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The policy page doesn't mention AI or LLMs explicitly; whether summaries count as 'derived data' is our open question.

nuances.text: Quota is moving to per-method buckets (from June 1, 2026), and upload cost dropped from about 1,600 units to about 100 units (Dec 2025); videos.insert now costs 1 unit in its own 100-call bucket.
Videos uploaded from unverified API projects are no longer restricted to private; uploads default to public unless creator account settings say otherwise.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Older guidance said unaudited projects created after July 28, 2020 uploaded private-only; the current videos.insert page says otherwise.

nuances.text: Quota is per Cloud project and resets at midnight Pacific; there is no paid tier to buy more.
After a merger, acquisition or other change of control you must file a Change of Control form, and YouTube may run periodic re-audits at any time.
